annotation.authors_or_issuer: Basu, S.; Omotubora, A.; Fox, C.
key_provisions_or_claims: ADRs could be treated as pedestrians under existing law.
Game theory requires credible threats of small harm to avoid the freezing robot problem.
Proposes robot self-defence and right to property as legal basis for small penalties.
Examines criminal and civil liability for deliberate or accidental collisions.
Raises privacy and data protection issues from modelling pedestrian interactions.
annotation.summary_en: Legal analysis arguing autonomous delivery robots could be treated as pedestrians and could lawfully inflict game-theoretic small penalties on pedestrians, grounded in robot self-defence and property rights. It examines criminal and civil liability for collisions and privacy issues, and calls for stakeholder consultation and legal reform.
annotation.title_clean: Autonomous delivery robots: a legal framework for infliction of game-theoretic small penalties on pedestrians
annotation.title_en: Autonomous delivery robots: a legal framework for infliction of game-theoretic small penalties on pedestrians
